title: Events at a Site Where the Client Holds Other Larkspur Table Programmes
content:
What a client holds elsewhere in the dining programme changes what an event under Private Event & Banquet Services costs and who produces it.

## Production out of a cafe kitchen

Where the same client holds an active Workplace Cafe Management Program contract at the site the venue sits in, and that contract's service model permits catering out of the cafe kitchen, the event is produced in that kitchen and no preferred vendor fee is charged for the food.

Where the client brings an outside caterer into a venue at a site where they already hold a cafe contract permitting catering, the preferred vendor fee printed against the package is charged in full, because the in-house kitchen was available and was not used.

| At a site with a cafe contract permitting catering | Preferred vendor fee on the food |
| --- | --- |
| The event is produced in the cafe kitchen | None charged |
| An outside caterer is brought in | Charged in full at the package's percentage |

## The room and the catering agreement

The following clause is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis: "A private event and banquet booking and a corporate catering order for the same room on the same day are mutually exclusive: the room is held by the booking, and any additional food for that room is added to the event rather than ordered through the catering agreement."

Where the client holds a Corporate Catering Service Agreement whose largest guest count is smaller than the event's guaranteed count, the event stays on the event services agreement whatever the client asks, since only the venue can seat it.

## Where the cafe contract lapses

Where the cafe contract at the site closes or stands suspended, production moves to the district kitchen and the event price is unchanged, since the package rate already covers production.
